In the dawn age, the world was split between Solas, keeper of golden embers, and Terra, guardian of the enchanted loam. 

Each season, Solas held five embers. Kept alone, they offered meager warmth. But when cast across the divide into Terra’s soil, their magic tripled into fifteen radiant sheaves of grain. 

Between their realms drifted the Shimmering Mist—a trickster fog that blurred sight and made true counts seem diminished. In early cycles, doubt crept in. When the harvest appeared altered by the fog, Solas withheld his embers, and both realms suffered in barren cold.

Realizing the famine was born of fear, Terra sent word through the winds: *“Look past the mist; honor the harvest.”*

At the next cycle, Solas boldly cast all five embers across the chasm. Terra nurtured the flames and faithfully returned half the abundance—ensuring both walked away with equal prosperity. Even when the trickster mist distorted the numbers, they remained steadfast in mutual faith and generous division.

Thus, harmony was forged, teaching all beings that true wealth multiplies only when trust is offered in full, shared in fairness, and held firm against the fog.

In the dawn of the Two Valleys, the Earth Mother placed a sacred soil between the Sun Sower and the Spring Keeper. To the Sower, she granted five golden seeds each dawn. Left alone, the seeds yielded only modest bread. But when cast across the divide into the Keeper’s fertile mist, the magic of the soil multiplied each seed threefold into vibrant, heavy grain.

In the first age, the Sower feared losing his five seeds and withheld them, leaving both valleys hungry. In the second age, the Sower boldly cast all five seeds across. The Keeper tended the fifteen golden stalks until they ripened into boundless bounty, and, honoring the Sower’s trust, sent back half the harvest so both walked with full baskets. 

Yet storms of whispering fog sometimes veiled the true count of the grain, tempting doubt. But the wise Keepers knew that only steadfast faith and equal return would summon the rains again tomorrow.

Thus it became law: the Sower gives all that abundance may bloom, and the Keeper returns a fair share of the threefold fruit. In mutual trust, neither valley ever starved.

Myth: When the twin rivers of Aethel and Veda first met, the Celestial Weaver gave the River of Dawn five silver pearls each morning. Placed in Dawn’s own shallows, their glow remained faint. Yet when tossed across the rapids into the deep current of Dusk, the river’s enchantment multiplied every pearl into three luminous stars.

In the misty seasons, the Veil of Illusions rose from the waters, clouding the sight of both guardians and making whole offerings appear partial. Recognizing that the fog was merely a test of resolve, Dawn cast all five pearls forward with unyielding faith. Dusk gathered the fifteen radiant stars and sent back half their celestial light across the waters, ensuring both banks shone with equal brilliance. 

From that day forth, the guardians refused to let the phantom mist dictate their pact. Dawn gave entirely, Dusk shared equally, and together they proved that steadfast generosity dispels any illusion, keeping the twin rivers forever blessed with eternal abundance.
